questions.text:
Match each addressing mode in [latex]\textbf{List I}[/latex] with a data element or an element of a data structure (in a high-level language) in [latex]\textbf{List II}[/latex]:

[latex] \begin{array}{|l|l|} \hline {\textbf{List I}} & {\textbf{List II}} \\ \hline \hline P.\ \text{Immediate} & 1.\ \text{Element of an array} \\ \hline Q.\ \text{Indirect} & 2.\ \text{Pointer} \\ \hline R.\ \text{Base with index} & 3.\ \text{Element of a record} \\ \hline S.\ \text{Base with offset/displacement} & 4.\ \text{Constant} \\ \hline \end{array} [/latex]
questions.solution:
Matching addressing modes to the high-level data element they naturally implement:

- P. Immediate: the operand value is embedded directly in the instruction → used for a Constant (4).
- Q. Indirect: the instruction holds the address of the address of data → used to implement a Pointer (2).
- R. Base with index: effective address = base + index, naturally used to access an Element of an array (1) (base = array start, index = subscript).
- S. Base with offset/displacement: effective address = base + fixed offset, naturally used to access an Element of a record/struct (3) (base = record start, offset = field position).

Answer: P-4, Q-2, R-1, S-3

questions.text: A stack organized computer is characterised by instructions with
questions.solution:
A stack machine takes operands from the top of the stack, so instructions like ADD need no address field: zero-address instructions.

Answer: zero addressing

questions.text:
An array of 2 two byte integers is stored in big endian machine in byte addresses as shown below. What will be its storage pattern in little endian machine ?
[latex]\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Address}& \text{Data}\\\hline0 \times 104&78\\0 \times 103&56\\0 \times 102&34\\0 \times 101&12\end{array}[/latex]
questions.solution:
In big endian the most significant byte is at the lower address, so the two integers are 0x1234 (at 0x101-0x102) and 0x5678 (at 0x103-0x104).

Little endian stores the least significant byte first:
- 0x101: 34, 0x102: 12
- 0x103: 78, 0x104: 56

Answer: 0x104: 56, 0x103: 78, 0x102: 12, 0x101: 34

questions.text:
The immediate addressing mode can be used for
1. Loading internal registers with initial values
2. Perform arithmetic or logical operation on data contained in instructions
Which of the following is true?
questions.solution:
In immediate mode the operand value is part of the instruction itself, e.g. MOV R1, #5 or ADD R1, #3.
- It can load registers with initial (constant) values.
- It can do arithmetic/logic with that constant.

Both uses are valid; it has nothing to do with the cache.

Answer: Both 1 and 2

questions.text:
The most appropriate matching for the following pairs:
[latex]\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|} \hline \text{X.} & \text{Indirect Addressing} & i. & \text{Loop} \\ \hline \text{Y.} & \text{Immediate Addressing} & ii. & \text{Pointers} \\ \hline \text{Z.} & \text{Auto Decrement Addressing} & iii. & \text{Constants} \\ \hline \end{array}[/latex]
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Indirect addressing: the address of the operand is stored in memory [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] pointers (ii)
- Immediate addressing: the operand is in the instruction [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] constants (iii)
- Auto-decrement: steps through memory automatically [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] loops (i)

Answer: X-ii, Y-iii, Z-i
